selected_result: Blanchard–Higham–Mary Theorem 4.1: per-product backward-error representation for an inner product computed using FABsum

bibliographic_source.title: A Class of Fast and Accurate Summation Algorithms

paper_locations.anchor: Working-precision product error model, complete FABsum algorithm, and per-input summation backward-error constants epsilon_f, epsilon_a
Apply FABsum to rounded products; computed dot product is sum x_i*y_i*(1+mu_i), with first-order coefficient u+epsilon_a(n/b)+epsilon_f(b)

task_clarification: For each admissible n,b with b>0 dividing n, first compute rounded products z_i=fl(x_i*y_i), then apply full Algorithm 3.1 FABsum to those z_i using a paper-admissible FastSum and AccurateSum with their stated per-input backward-error contracts epsilon_f and epsilon_a.

Formalize existence of per-product perturbations mu_i such that the returned dot product equals sum_i x_i*y_i*(1+mu_i), uniformly bounded with the source's first-order coefficient u+epsilon_a(n/b)+epsilon_f(b) and the corresponding explicit higher-order terms or a mathematically justified finite-u strengthening.

The result is a generic Algorithm 4.1 theorem over the FastSum/AccurateSum contracts from Theorem 3.1, not only one preselected summation method. Source review must check whether those contracts alone suffice to specify the actual computation without assuming the target result.
scope_constraints: Do not omit the initial rounded products or silently use exact products; retain arbitrary signs and cancellation.
Do not state only a scalar absolute forward-error bound; preserve the per-product backward-error representation.
Do not assume the complete dot-product bound as an input hypothesis; only the paper's lower-level FastSum/AccurateSum bounds are admissible.

The source's epsilon notation includes asymptotic O(u^2). If formalizing at fixed u, provide a precise finite-u coefficient with appropriate positivity and smallness guards; do not treat O(u^2) as a literal numeric constant.
Use genuine multiplication and addition operations from the floating-point model and the complete block algorithm; retain source overflow/underflow conditions.
